articles.title: A pragmatic clinical definition of traumatic shock using systolic blood pressure and shock index: A national registry study.
articles.authors: Noonan M, O'Reilly G, Balogh ZJ, Mathew J, Ellis DY, Groombridge C, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national trauma registry data
articles.population: Adult major trauma patients in Australia and New Zealand
articles.sample_size: 47,730 patients in hospital arrival analysis; 31,267 in pre-hospital analysis
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality, emergency department mortality, rates of operative intervention, intensive care unit and acute hospital length of stay
articles.take_home: Patients with signs of traumatic shock (low blood pressure or high shock index) had substantially higher death rates in hospital compared to those without shock. Those with the lowest blood pressure readings had the worst outcomes and needed more surgery and longer hospital stays.

articles.title: Same-day discharge does not increase complications or readmissions in carefully selected patients undergoing aseptic lower extremity nonunion surgery.
articles.authors: Lauck BJ, Paterno AV, Suh YM, Odum S, Rice O, Averkamp BJ, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study across 14 Level 1 trauma centres
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing surgical fixation of aseptic femur or tibia nonunions
articles.outcomes: Postoperative infection rates, readmission rates, and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: In carefully selected patients, same-day discharge after surgery for lower leg bone nonunions did not lead to more infections, readmissions or need for further surgery compared with staying in hospital overnight. This suggests same-day discharge can be safe for appropriate patients undergoing this type of surgery.

articles.title: The Articular Dislocation Angle of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint: Its Conception, Measurement Method, and Role in Hallux Valgus.
articles.authors: Guo M, Liu F, Gan Y, Yang F
articles.study_type: Diagnostic study introducing a new measurement method
articles.population: Patients with hallux valgus (bunions), predominantly female and Asian
articles.sample_size: 70 feet from 52 patients, mean age 58 years
articles.outcomes: Introduction of articular dislocation angle (ADA) measurement; quantification of how different anatomical factors contribute to hallux valgus; comparison of weight-bearing radiographs versus CT scan accuracy
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a new measurement called the articular dislocation angle to assess how much joint dislocation contributes to bunion deformity. As bunions become more severe, joint dislocation becomes increasingly important (accounting for 43% in mild cases up to 69% in severe cases), helping surgeons plan appropriate surgery.

articles.title: Robotic-arm-assisted versus conventional total knee replacement (RACER-Knee): a pragmatic, multicentre, participant-masked and assessor-masked, superiority, randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Parsons H, Metcalfe A, Griffin J, Khatri C, Bradley H, Blyth M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with advanced knee osteoarthritis undergoing total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Forgotten Joint Score at 12 months; cost-effectiveness; serious adverse events
articles.take_home: Robotic-arm-assisted knee replacement did not provide better patient outcomes than conventional surgery at 12 months and was more costly, though both approaches were equally safe.

articles.title: Short-to Medium-term Results of Displaced Femoral Neck Fractures in Patients Less than 50 Years of Age Undergoing Repair: Comparison of Open vs. Closed Reduction.
articles.authors: Collinge C, Wong H, Patterson J, Finlay A, Gardner M, Lebus GF, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged under 50 years with displaced femoral neck fractures undergoing surgical repair
articles.outcomes: Major complications including nonunion, failed fixation, osteonecrosis, malunion and need for reconstructive surgery
articles.take_home: Both open and closed reduction methods for femoral neck fractures in young patients resulted in similar rates of complications and repair failure. The choice of reduction method did not significantly affect outcomes over short to medium-term follow-up.

articles.title: Outcomes of One-Stage Infected Humerus Nonunion Repair in Patients with Prior Operative Fracture Fixation.
articles.authors: Katzir A, Bilodeau RE, Bhadouriya RS, Kantor AH, Schlauch A, Klinger CE, et al.
articles.population: Patients with infected humerus nonunion following failed prior surgical fixation
articles.outcomes: Union achievement, infection eradication, number of surgeries needed, and antibiotic therapy duration
articles.take_home: One-stage repair for infected humerus nonunion achieved union in 87% of patients, but one in three patients needed further surgery for recurrent infection or ongoing nonunion. Two-thirds of patients achieved union with the initial repair alone.

articles.title: Evaluating the efficacy of disinfecting agents against Staphylococcus aureus on external fixator devices.
articles.authors: Horowitz ME, Talsania A, Grando K, Walters T, Albicoro FJ, Tukel C, et al.
articles.population: External fixator devices colonised with Staphylococcus aureus bacteria
articles.outcomes: Bacterial colony forming units (CFUs) remaining after disinfection; frequency of zero versus detectable CFU counts
articles.take_home: All four disinfectants tested significantly reduced bacteria on external fixators compared to untreated controls, with no meaningful difference between them. Chlorhexidine Gluconate plus isopropyl alcohol showed the most consistent sterilisation, whilst Betadine plus isopropyl alcohol was less reliable.

articles.title: Validity of the non-union scoring system in management of long bone fracture non-union. A prospective study.
articles.authors: Wafa TA, Al Kersh MA, Ghaly NAM, Ahmed AR, Rizk MH, Mahran MA
articles.population: Patients with femoral and tibial non-union (both septic and aseptic)
articles.outcomes: Union rates by treatment group (Group 1: 88.9%, Group 2: 80%, Group 3: 81.5%) and time to clinical and radiographic healing
articles.take_home: The Non-union Scoring System is a reliable tool for guiding treatment of long bone non-union, though it sometimes underestimates how much treatment a patient needs. Adding checks during surgery can help ensure patients get the right level of treatment.

articles.title: Risk stratification in older adults with rib fractures: Performance of the STUMBL score.
articles.authors: Bui A, Gregorevic K, Read D, Lim WK
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years and over with traumatic rib fractures
articles.outcomes: 3-month mortality, delirium, 12-month mortality, length of stay, functional decline, and failure to return to usual place of residence
articles.take_home: The STUMBL score reliably predicts which older patients with rib fractures are at higher risk of death, delirium, and loss of independence. Using this score alongside assessments of frailty and thinking ability may help clinicians plan care earlier and involve specialist geriatric services when needed.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and temporal trends of adult acute compartment syndrome From 2015 to 2025.
articles.authors: Ruppert NF, Sanghvi PA, Good LM, Florentino SA, Berk AN, Adelstein JM, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study analysing a large national database
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over who underwent fasciotomy for acute compartment syndrome
articles.sample_size: 10,045 patients with acute compartment syndrome identified from 117,592,405 patients in the TriNetX database
articles.outcomes: Incidence of acute compartment syndrome, patient demographics, associated injuries, anatomic location, medical complications including readmission and acute kidney injury within 30 days, and mortality at 7 and 30 days
articles.take_home: Acute compartment syndrome is rare, affecting about 33 per million people per year, with rates stable over the decade studied. Most cases involve lower limb fractures in middle-aged men, and nearly half of patients need readmission within 30 days, with a 6% mortality rate at one month.

articles.title: Epidemiology, associated injuries, and surgical intervention of 255,081 clavicle fractures in the United States from 2015 to 2024.
articles.authors: Rodio LA, Adelstein JM, Burkhart RJ, Good LM, Moyal AJ, Napora JK
articles.population: Patients with clavicle fractures in the United States
articles.outcomes: Incidence rates by age and sex; associated injuries; rates of surgical intervention (ORIF)
articles.take_home: Clavicle fractures are increasing in the US, occurring more often in men and in people under 19 or over 80 years old. About 7.5% are treated with surgery, with surgery most common in people aged 20 to 29 and least common in young children and elderly patients.

articles.title: Operative and non-operative management of people with hip fracture: A modified-Delphi study to develop an international consensus.
articles.authors: Mitchell RJ, Johansen A, Willems HC, Tabu I, Seymour H, Moppett I
articles.population: International panel of healthcare professionals (anaesthetists, orthopaedic/trauma surgeons, geriatricians) from 17 countries
articles.outcomes: 15 consensus statements on operative and non-operative management of hip fracture; 14 achieved high consensus (≥70% agreement) and 1 moderate consensus (50-69% agreement)
articles.take_home: Experts from multiple countries have agreed on statements to guide hip fracture treatment decisions, whether surgical or non-surgical. The final choice should be tailored to each patient's individual circumstances rather than following a one-size-fits-all approach.

articles.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in adult trauma patients with flail chest with or without severe traumatic brain injury: A national analysis.
articles.authors: Nasef H, Chin B, Nunes N, Werling A, Amin Q, Wright DD, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis using national trauma registry data
articles.population: Adult trauma patients with flail chest, analysed separately for those without brain injury and those with severe traumatic brain injury
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality, intensive care unit length of stay, ventilator-free days, ventilator-associated pneumonia, tracheostomy, and discharge destination
articles.take_home: For patients with flail chest alone, surgery to stabilise rib fractures did not improve survival compared to non-surgical treatment. However, for patients with both flail chest and severe brain injury, surgical stabilisation was associated with lower death rates, though both groups had longer intensive care stays and higher rates of complications like pneumonia when treated surgically.

articles.title: Cytokine release after geriatric coxal monotrauma.
articles.authors: Pass B, Boerner A, Bousch JF, Schoeps D, Maus U, Kupschus J, et al.
articles.population: Older adults (aged over 70) with proximal femur fractures, older adults undergoing elective hip replacement, and young healthy controls (under 50 years)
articles.outcomes: Blood levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-10 (IL-10), and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) measured before surgery and on days 0, 1, 4, and 7 after surgery
articles.take_home: Older patients with hip fractures had higher inflammation markers before surgery compared to those having planned hip replacements, suggesting fracture trauma triggers a stronger pre-operative inflammatory response. Measuring these inflammation markers might help doctors identify older patients at higher risk after hip surgery.

articles.title: Protocol for the ACTIVE trial: a multicentre, open-label, cluster-randomized controlled trial of a quality improvement programme for older adults with hip fracture in resource-limited hospitals in China.
articles.authors: Yang M, Liu T, Liu G, Tang N, Zhang X, Ivers R, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years or older with acute unilateral hip fracture in less-resourced hospitals in China
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: health-related quality of life at 120 days after admission. Secondary outcomes: quality of life at 30 days, complications and morbidity at 30 and 120 days, proportion having surgery, proportion on full weightbearing at one week post-surgery, time from admission to surgery, length of hospital stay, 120-day mortality, and inpatient costs
articles.take_home: This study will test whether a tailored quality improvement programme that optimises hospital management, empowers doctors, and educates patients can improve outcomes for older adults with hip fracture in under-resourced Chinese hospitals. The results will show whether this approach helps people recover better within 120 days of admission.

articles.title: Maximizing stem body size may reduce the risk of postoperative periprosthetic fractures : an analysis of 2,757 CPT femoral components.
articles.authors: van Duren BH, Firth AM, France J, Nightingale J, Bloch BV, Manktelow AR, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip replacement with polished taper slip femoral components
articles.outcomes: Postoperative periprosthetic fractures (breaks in bone around the implant); identified 40 fractures (1.45%) at mean 6.4 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Older age and certain implant design features increase the risk of fractures around hip replacements. Using a larger implant stem relative to the offset (positioning) of the hip joint appears to reduce fracture risk.

articles.title: The Surgeon-Jurist: Reclaiming Judgment in an Era of Defensive Medicine.
articles.authors: Salphale YS
articles.take_home: Good orthopaedic care requires surgeons to use clinical judgment to apply evidence-based guidelines flexibly to individual patients' needs and preferences, rather than following protocols rigidly or practising defensively.

articles.title: High-dose melatonin for early tibial fracture healing: A prospective study of safety, feasibility, and preliminary biological effects.
articles.authors: Ninomiya AF, Bertolucci V, Nonose N, Messias LO, Beck WR, Pejon TMM, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18-60 years with closed tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nailing
articles.outcomes: Serum alkaline phosphatase levels and radiographic union scores at 21 and 49 days; adverse events and sleep quality
articles.take_home: High-dose melatonin (30 mg daily) was safe and well tolerated after tibial fracture surgery, but did not speed up bone healing in the first seven weeks compared to standard care. Both groups showed normal healing progression regardless of melatonin use.

articles.title: Phantom limb pain and associated factors in traumatic amputees: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Artuc SE, Kilinc Kamaci G, Sahan HF, Cetinturk H, Demir Y, Aydemir K
articles.population: Traumatic amputees (mean age 35.2 years) rehabilitated at a tertiary hospital, with injuries from firearms, landmines, natural disasters and traffic accidents
articles.outcomes: Prevalence and severity of phantom limb pain measured on a Visual Analog Scale; associations between age, clinical variables and pain severity, frequency and daily impact
articles.take_home: Phantom limb pain affected 61% of traumatic amputees with an average severity score of 6.46 out of 10. Older age was weakly linked to greater pain severity, but other clinical factors did not clearly predict how often pain occurred or how much it affected daily life.

articles.title: Outcomes of a physiotherapy performed trauma tertiary survey role on a dedicated trauma ward in a Level 1 trauma service.
articles.authors: Webb M, Holland A, Noonan M, Kirk A, Calthorpe S, Mathew J, et al.
articles.population: Trauma patients admitted to a Level 1 trauma centre in Australia
articles.sample_size: 1147 patients in intervention phase, 591 in baseline phase
articles.outcomes: Timeliness of trauma tertiary survey (median time to completion), injury detection rates, safety, rates of survey completion on discharge day
articles.take_home: When senior physiotherapists performed trauma surveys alongside doctors, surveys were completed faster (27 hours instead of 41 hours) and fewer were left until discharge. Physiotherapists found 120 injuries, mainly musculoskeletal problems, without compromising patient safety.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of the femoral neck system, cannulated cancellous screws combined with medial buttress plate, and cannulated cancellous screws in the treatment of femoral neck fractures in young and middle-aged adults.
articles.authors: Huang Y, Lin J, Chen X, Li R, Jiang X, Lin D, et al.
articles.population: Young and middle-aged adults aged 18-65 years with femoral neck fractures
articles.outcomes: Fracture healing time, Harris Hip Score, Oxford Hip Score, complication rates including femoral neck shortening and osteonecrosis
articles.take_home: Adding a buttress plate to screws helped patients recover function faster in the first three months, but all three surgical approaches produced similar results by six months and beyond. None of the three methods was clearly better overall, so the choice should be tailored to individual patient circumstances.

articles.title: Dorsal subchondral arc line: A novel radiographic marker to avoid dorsal screw prominence during distal radius fixation with volar locking plates.
articles.authors: Worhacz K, Castaneda P, Hui C, Walker JB
articles.population: Matched pairs of cadaveric forearms
articles.outcomes: Dorsal cortex penetration, stiffness, and load to failure under cyclical and ultimate axial compression
articles.take_home: A new measurement method called the Dorsal Subchondral Arc Line can help surgeons choose the right screw length during wrist fracture surgery to avoid screws poking through the back of the bone, whilst still providing equivalent strength to longer screws that go all the way through.
